pages.text: Down in Hazelwood somebody is coughing. Then somebody else. The children first, as always, and nobody knows what to do.
Wren the healer comes up the road with a full basket. “I cannot do this alone, {player},” she says. “Berit's old still-room is behind your kitchen. Would you look?”

c5_stillroom.title: A torn page
c5_stillroom.text: Under the last shelf lies a page, torn in two. The top half is in a tidy hand: “Tea first. Always tea first.” The bottom half is missing. Somebody was here before you, and cared.

pages.text: Wren is waiting at the edge of the forest with her arms folded. “One rule,” she says. “Bring me your basket. Every time. Before you use anything in it.”
“Plants have twins, and some twins are poison. I do not care how clever you are. I care that you wake up tomorrow.” She almost smiles. “It costs a little favour. A biscuit will do.”

c5_conch.title: Something white
c5_conch.text: Far off between the trees, something white and spiral shines in the green. It does not move. You hold your breath. Then you go back to your basket. Some things are for later.

c5_first_tea.title: A pupil for Wren
c5_first_tea.text: Greenstem, the boy from the market, stands in the doorway of the still-room and sniffs. “Can I learn this?” Wren grumbles something about boys and mud. Then she says yes.

pages.text: The ceiling. A blanket. A cup of something bitter. Wren sits by your bed, and she is not smiling. “What were you thinking?” she says. Your purse is gone. Your legs shake.
“You are well,” she says. “That is all that matters. Next time, the basket comes to me first.” She puts a hand on your head, very briefly, and goes to stir her pot.

c5_page.title: The other half
c5_page.text: The chest is full. In its lid, rolled up, you find the other half of the torn page: “The badger left after the fever, when nobody let the children rest.” You read it twice. You were one of those children.

c5_collapse.title: You never stop
c5_collapse.text: You make one more tea, and one more, day and night. Then the pot tilts and the floor comes up. Wren finds you on the stone. “You never stop, do you?” she says, and carries you to the bench.

pages.text: At the door of the still-room sits a badger, with his back very straight. He looks at the chest. He looks at the tea set. Then he looks at you, and at your hands.
He sets out two cups. “Tea first,” he seems to say. You sit down. For the first time in a long time, you do nothing at all. The badger pours.

c5_letter.title: A letter with a seal
c5_letter.text: A boy runs up the road with a letter. The seal is red wax, pressed with a heavy ring. “From the Lord,” he pants. You do not open it yet. The badger looks at it, and then at you, and says nothing.
